newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler sees good chance of German EMS qualifying.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler sees good chance of German EMS qualifying.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said despite Germany's relatively high new public borrowing in 1996, he saw a good chance that it would qualify for monetary union.

Zeitler, who is also president of the state central bank of Bavaria, told Bayerischer Rundfunk in an interview that fulfilling the convergence criteria took precedence over sticking to the timetable and trying to get as many states as possible into the planned currency union.
"The principle remains that quality must have priority over the other aims," Zeitler said.
He also said he saw no reason to expect an increase in interest rates linked to the launch of European monetary union, scheduled for January 1, 1999.
